text.p: Telefonos de Mexico American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) rose on Tuesday, helped in part by a ratings upgrade from Smith Barney.
ADRs in New York were trading without strong marketwide momentum, traders said.
"We're seeing various features in various countries, but we're not seeing the whole market moving," a trader said. "It feels strange here."

Brazilian telecommunications holding Telebras rose 5/8 to 100-3/8 boosted by a judge's decision to throw out a request for an order aimed at blocking the government's plans to sell off cellular phone concessions.
Australia's News Corp ADRs for ordinary shares rose 3/8 to 21-5/8 in heavy volume. Its preferred shares were up 3/4 to 18-1/4, also in heavy trade.
News Corp announced on Monday a direct satellite broadcast alliance with EchoStar Communications Corp.
Advancers led decliners by 255 to 240 among 807 ADRs. Volume was 41 million shares at midday.

Telefonos de Mexico, or Telmex, was up 3/8 to 40-1/2 after Smith Barney raised its rating for the one-time monopoly to outperform from market perform. The rise also came as the Mexican stock market hit an intraday record.
Telmex volume at midday was 1.7 million shares, putting Telmex among the active ADRs on the New York Stock Exchange.

Mexican bottler Coca-Cola FEMSA SA rose 2-5/8 to 35 in heavy volume after UBS Securities started coverage of the company as a buy. Coca-Cola FEMSA reported increased fourth quarter sales and profits on Monday.
